emma_cs: Hey team — AcmeCorp is hitting a sudden surge of 504s and a few 502s on hosted inference starting ~2026-03-16T10:12Z. Affects both streaming and non-streaming calls to redwood-v1-large in us-west-2. Customer correlation id: acme-9f4b. ~40% of requests returning 504 within their load tests. Escalating for urgent triage.

priya_sre: Can you paste a minimal repro, SDK version, and the correlation id (thanks). Is this only streaming? Any recent customer config changes or batching spikes? We'll start checking gateway/edge logs.

josh_eng: Also include a curl repro + exact headers. Suspect HTTP/2 stream resets or LB keepalive evictions. Will grep gateway logs for acme-9f4b.

emma_cs: Repro and logs below. SDK is node v3.4.1. Streaming and non-streaming both fail sometimes.

```bash
# curl repro (non-streaming)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-large","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

```js
// node SDK repro (non-streaming)
const res = await Redwood.generate({ model: 'redwood-v1-large', input: 'hello', stream: false });
console.log(res);
```

Logs (edge/gateway):
```
edge-gateway[2026-03-16T10:12:15Z] corr=acme-9f4b upstream_status=504 error="connection closed while reading upstream"
edge-gateway[2026-03-16T10:12:15Z] socket=xyz h2_stream_reset=1
upstream[2026-03-16T10:12:15Z] backend=runner-3 status=504 body="upstream timeout"
client-sdk[2026-03-16T10:12:16Z] retry=1 status=504
client-sdk[2026-03-16T10:12:17Z] retry=2 status=504
```

emma_cs: Customer also attached their SDK logs showing a short retry loop (3 attempts) then final 504. They are on our hosted tier and are sensitive to latency spikes.

josh_eng: Thanks — I'm pulling gateway traces for corr=acme-9f4b and the 10:12 window. @max_reliability did we roll anything around 03:50Z in us-west-2?

max_reliability: We did push a small change at 03:50Z that reduced LB idle keepalive from 90s -> 30s to improve churn. That can cause unexpected h2 stream resets for multiplexed clients that hold connections. I'll roll a canary rollback and check metrics. Also noticed Acme was sending large embedding batches earlier (batch_size=512) which increases head-of-line pressure.

priya_sre: Opening P0 ticket to infra now. Mitigation options: 1) temporary routing of Acme to us-east-1, 2) ask Acme to increase client-side retry/backoff (base=200ms, max=6s) with jitter, 3) recommend disabling HTTP/2 multiplexing or force HTTP/1.1 for now.

emma_cs: Pasting draft customer message for review: "Hi Acme — we see a spike of gateway timeouts in us-west-2 impacting some requests. We're routing your traffic to us-east-1 temporarily and asking you to enable a slightly longer retry backoff in your SDK. We're investigating and will update within 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption." :pray:

infra-bot: INC-7891 created (priority=P0) — assigned to infra-team.

josh_eng: Quick workaround for the SDK while we stabilize: set header `Connection: close` or env `REDWOOD_FORCE_HTTP1=true` to avoid h2 multiplexing, or set sdk option `transport: "http1"`. Example: `curl -H 'Connection: close' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' ...`

max_reliability: Rolled a canary rollback of the keepalive change at 10:55Z in us-west-2 and created a traffic policy to route Acme -> us-east-1 temporarily (applied 11:02Z). Monitoring.

emma_cs: Customer reports errors dropped to <1% after routing at 11:05Z, confirming improvement. I'll keep them in the loop and close the temporary mitigation once stable.

sanjay_support: I'll send the formal customer update and propose a conversation about Dedicated capacity or reserved routing if they want sustained reduction.

emma_cs: Final update for thread: temporary route applied, canary rollback initiated, INC-7891 open. Infra will follow up with RCA & postmortem. Closing thread unless new errors crop up. :white_check_mark:
